specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** reuse-evidence-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** assess
**Learning Objective:** The learner will assess eight signals as strong evidence of reuse, weak evidence, or not evidence of reuse, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Reuse Tracking, Derivative Work, Component Licensing (defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapter 15). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each signal the learner commits one of three bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the three strengths is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Page views measure reuse. (2) A star on a repository is a use. (3) All visits come from readers. **Instructional Rationale:** Assessing the strength of evidence is an Evaluate-level action. Signals that show use, interest, and nothing at all teach the learner not to count every number as impact. **Content:** The three bins: Strong evidence of reuse, Weak evidence, Not evidence of reuse. The eight signals (all made up, for Watershed Basics v1.1): | # | Signal | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | A teacher's course page embeds your simulation and credits you. | Strong evidence of reuse | Someone is using it and has credited it. | | 2 | Someone copied your repository and changed the quiz. | Strong evidence of reuse | A copy with changes is an adaptation. | | 3 | An email says, "I used your reading with my class and added two questions." | Strong evidence of reuse | A user describes using and adapting it. | | 4 | The clearinghouse listing shows 300 downloads. | Weak evidence | A download shows interest and not use. | | 5 | The site had 1,200 page views last month. | Weak evidence | A view shows a visit and not reuse. | | 6 | Three people starred your repository. | Weak evidence | A star shows interest. | | 7 | Your own computer opened the site 40 times while you tested it. | Not evidence of reuse | The visits are yours. | | 8 | Traffic spiked when automated crawlers scanned the site. | Not evidence of reuse | No reader was involved. | **Provenance:** The signals are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The strengths follow the chapter section "Reuse Tracking". **Rules:** Each signal has exactly one correct bin. Three signals are Strong evidence of reuse, three are Weak evidence, and two are Not evidence of reuse. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one signal and the three bins. 2. The learner places the signal in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After signal 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 signals in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can weigh signs of reuse." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed signal. **Starting State:** The first signal in the shuffled order and the three bins. The question shown is "Does this show that someone reused the resource?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists strong signals, weak signals, and non-evidence.
